# Outline {.unnumbered}

## Author {.unnumbered}

My name is Ahmad Daryanto (Anto). I am the module leader and developed this website. This is my personal website [https://sites.google.com/view/ahmaddaryanto/](https://sites.google.com/view/ahmaddaryanto/)

## Aim {.unnumbered}

At the end of the course, I want you to say this: I love marketing and don't avoid numbers. 

## Learning Objectives {.unnumbered}

1.	To improve basic numeracy skills and understand basic statistical concepts (statistics in MKTG200)

2.	To increase students’ appreciation of the importance of gaining those skills in the marketing environment

3.	As a preparation for advanced modules in Part 2


## How to Study {.unnumbered}
In learning a topic, in a section covering the topic, your learning journey is described by this flowchart:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Problem] --> B{Got it?}
  B --> D[Yes]
  D --> F[Go to 'Your Turn']
  B --> E[No]
  E --> G[Watch Video]
  G --> F[Go to 'Your Turn']
```

## Program Structure {.unnumbered}

The module runs from week 5 - 8 in the Michaelmas term.

## Contents {.unnumbered}

| Week | Topic |  
|:----:|:----:|
| 5  | Arithmetic  of whole numbers  |   
| 5  | Fraction  |   
| 5  | Decimal numbers  |   
| 6  | Percentage and ratio  |   
| 6  | Algebra	  |   
| 7  | Indices	  |   
| 7  | Simplifying algebraic expressions  |   
| 8  | Functions	  |   
  

## Textbook {.unnumbered}

No textbook is needed. But if you want to buy a book, I recommend @Dar2020. This is a compilation book (I don't create it!) in which the chapters are taken from @Croft2006 and @Berenson2012 (Honestly, this is my quickest route of having a book with my name on it). I used this book in the past but realized that students were complaining the book was too thin to put under their pillows. 

## Excel {.unnumbered}

I provide `Excel` command to answer problems where appropriate. This is a nice tool but also dangerous. Without an understanding, the use of `Excel` can put you in the dark forever. Therefore, make sure you understand how to solve problems manually before using `Excel`.
